items.title: Lionel Reason Interview, 1981-05-26
items.q: And I went on with Don. And I stayed with Don until 1939.

ctx.x: And, uh, he couldn't get any of them to play. And those were some of his special tunes. He figured they couldn't play that. They couldn't play anything else he had. So, when I went there, uh, I was still half asleep. So, he said, uh, play this for me. And, uh, I said, which, I said, this is the arrangement? He said, yeah. I said, man, I'm ready to rehearse right now. Let's go. And I went on it. And Don jumped up and Don, he said, this is what I've been trying to get you fellas to do all day. And the band is going…

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-12-30
items.q: That's when I got Lionel Reason in the band.

ctx.x: I had given up my band in New Orleans. That was the first time. And he confidants Beansy in backing me. Beansy had a son that he wanted to put in business.

So Beansy called me. Beansy and I have been great friends. I told him and I want to sell him out and you probably couldn't help him. I don't want the money, he says I just want him to learn the business. So he financed the deal for about $5,000 and bought this crook of automobile and he got on the road to book the band. He hadn't gotten as far as Austin when he had messed up about five or six days. But I organized my band again. That's when I got Lionel Reason in the band. I don't know if you ever heard of him a…

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: when I reorganized the band was Lionel Reason. Mm-hmm. That was the pianist.

ctx.x: Was he came in after Lloyd then?
Right. No, I, yes he did, after Lloyd. See, Lloyd didn't stay a long, long time. Jay Golson came in. And then from here when I reorganized the band was Lionel Reason. Mm-hmm. That was the pianist.
Did I ever get your father's name? Ferdinand.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-06-06
items.q: Then there was Lionel Reason, that's another pianist that's playing now. And I think that was the three pianists that I had.

ctx.x: That was later then. That is correct. Much later. That's when it was first recorded. Paul Gayton is the one that put it on. Then later on I got Camille Howard to play it but she played it in the wrong vein. She played it in the jump tempo and You Don't Love Me isn't a jump song. It was the theme song of the band. Cottrell, myself and Lloyd Glenn. The pianist that was in my band. He came after Freeman didn't he? Long after Freeman. Yes he came quite a while after Freeman. I think that, I'm not for sure I think…
You had a regular arranger for your band?
